bookTitle: Options, Futures, and Other Derivatives (John C. Hull)
generalAssumptions: Forward interest rates are mathematically implied by the current term structure of zero rates to prevent arbitrage.
An FRA is an OTC contract where cash settlement occurs at the start of the loan period discounted back from maturity.
Yield curves typically slope upward because investors require a liquidity premium for longer maturities (Liquidity Preference Theory).

facts.topic: Forward Interest Rate Under Continuous Compounding
facts.statement: The forward interest rate R_F for the period between future times T_1 and T_2 implied by continuous zero rates R_1 and R_2 is R_F = (R_2 * T_2 - R_1 * T_1) / (T_2 - T_1). If continuous zero rates increase with maturity, forward rates lie strictly above zero rates.

facts.statement: A forward loan starting at T_1 and maturing at T_2 can be synthetically locked today by borrowing for T_1 at rate R_1 and investing the proceeds for T_2 at rate R_2. If the market forward rate differs from R_F = (R_2*T_2 - R_1*T_1)/(T_2 - T_1), riskless arbitrage is achieved.

A Forward Rate Agreement (FRA) is an over-the-counter derivative contract designed to lock in an interest rate for a future lending or borrowing period between T_1 and T_2. The party paying fixed rate R_K receives floating rate R_M, hedging against rising interest rates.

facts.topic: FRA Payoff and Discounted Settlement at Time T_1
facts.statement: At maturity T_2, the payoff for an FRA paying fixed rate R_K on principal L is L * (R_M - R_K) * (T_2 - T_1). In practice, FRAs settle at time T_1, requiring the payoff to be discounted back at the market rate R_M: Settlement = L * (R_M - R_K) * (T_2 - T_1) / [1 + R_M * (T_2 - T_1)].

facts.topic: Valuation of an Existing FRA Prior to Maturity
facts.statement: An existing FRA that pays fixed rate R_K has value V_FRA = L * (R_F - R_K) * (T_2 - T_1) * e^(-R_2 * T_2), where R_F is the current forward rate for the period and R_2 is the risk-free discount zero rate for maturity T_2.

formulaDetails.name: FRA Value Prior to Maturity
formulaDetails.latex: V_{\text{FRA}} = L (R_F - R_K)(T_2 - T_1) e^{-R_2 T_2}

facts.topic: Theories of the Term Structure: Expectations vs Liquidity Preference
facts.statement: Expectations Theory asserts that forward rates equal expected future spot rates (R_F = E[R]). Liquidity Preference Theory proves that because lenders prefer short-term liquidity while borrowers prefer locking long-term debt, forward rates exceed expected future spot rates (R_F > E[R]) by a positive liquidity premium.

facts.statement: In 1994, Orange County treasurer Bob Citron used $7.5B in county equity to enter $13B in reverse repo borrowing, investing $20.5B in medium-term inverse floaters. When the Federal Reserve raised rates 6 times by 250 bps, repo funding costs exploded above asset yields, wiping out $1.6B and triggering municipal bankruptcy.

facts.statement: During the 2007-2009 financial crisis, banks hoarded liquidity due to subprime mortgage uncertainty, causing asset-backed commercial paper (ABCP) markets to freeze and the 3-month LIBOR-OIS spread to skyrocket to 364 bps, necessitating massive central bank term lending facilities.
